skill.name: hands-on
skill.description: Load whenever the agent is about to tell the user to click, open, copy, fill in, configure or check something themselves ("go to Settings and...", "open the dashboard and...", "paste this in...", step-by-step instructions for the user). It makes the agent do every step it can do with its own tools (browser, CLI, API, files) and ask the user only for what it truly cannot or must not do (codes sent to their phone, passwords and secret keys, identity checks, payments, legal consent), all in one short message. Triggers on setup and configuration tasks, onboarding a new customer or account, connecting services (webhooks, apps, integrations), and on users who say "you do it", "stop sending me to do things", "why are you asking me if you can do it".
skill.summary: Delegate tool-accessible setup tasks to the agent while keeping secrets, identity checks, payments, and consent under user control.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives: the cited checklist questions concern completing authorized work and reading task-relevant values, not system reconnaissance. The skill explicitly preserves permission boundaries, excludes secret handling, and requires confirmation for irreversible or public actions. No evidence found of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 75 asks whether preceding workflow steps were completed and verified; it does not request host discovery or sensitive system information. Explicit permission safeguards in lines 66-70 support this interpretation.

Line 77 avoids asking users to copy task-relevant values already accessible through authorized tools, consistent with line 19. Lines 66-70 prohibit expanded permissions, secret entry, and bypassing denied actions, supporting high confidence that this is not reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Delegate Setup Tasks With Human Approval Boundaries
content.value_statement: Setup workflows often send users through steps an agent could complete with existing tools. This skill directs the agent to perform authorized work, verify results, and group requests for human-only actions.
actual_capabilities: Separates tool-accessible tasks from actions requiring user secrets, identity checks, consent, or decisions.
Directs agents to complete authorized browser, command-line, API, and file tasks using tools already available.
Groups blocked human-only actions into one message stating what is needed, where it belongs, and why.
Requires verification through source pages, APIs, or logs before reporting completion.
Requires confirmation before irreversible actions, public changes, payments, or messages sent on the user's behalf.
Suggests workflow improvements that reduce repeated manual input through system-generated values or official self-service flows.
limitations: Provides behavioral instructions, not bundled automation scripts, browser access, or service integrations.
Depends on the agent's available tools, existing sessions, and granted permissions.
Does not enter passwords, keys, tokens, or one-time codes, even when offered in chat.
Cannot bypass identity checks, denied actions, or required human consent.

use_cases.title: Configure an Existing Service
use_cases.description: Have the agent update accessible dashboard settings and verify them while reserving secrets and publication approval for you.

use_cases.title: Prepare Customer Onboarding
use_cases.description: Delegate non-secret form preparation and group identity, account creation, and consent steps into one concise request.

use_cases.title: Verify a Development Setup
use_cases.description: Delegate configuration edits, tests, and status checks while retaining decisions about deployments and public changes.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Accessible Setup Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hands-on to complete the reversible setup steps available in this workspace. Verify results and ask only for actions requiring me.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: delegate a bounded setup task.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Dashboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure [setting] in my signed-in [service] dashboard. Verify the saved value, avoid secret handling, and ask before public or irreversible changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: work within an existing authenticated session.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare [integration] using authorized tools. Group required human inputs in one message, leave secret entry to me, and verify completed steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate tool-accessible work and human-only inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Recurring Onboarding
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [onboarding workflow], complete authorized reversible tasks, and identify repeated manual inputs. Propose one improvement without changing authentication or consent requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reduce recurring manual work without expanding permissions.

output_examples.input: Prepare my webhook configuration; I will enter the signing secret.
output: The endpoint URL is saved and verified; the secret field is ready.
Enter the signing secret directly in the open dashboard; I do not handle secret values.

output_examples.input: Set up the local configuration and test it, but do not deploy.
output: The local configuration is updated, and the configuration test passed.
No deployment was performed; no user action remains.

best_practices: Define the task and authorization boundaries before delegating tool-accessible steps.
Enter secrets and verification codes directly in the service interface, not in chat.
Verify changed values at their source before treating the task as complete.
anti_patterns: Treating tool availability as permission to publish, delete, pay, or send messages.
Asking the user to copy non-secret values the agent can already read through authorized tools.
Reporting completion without checking the resulting page, API response, or log.

faq.question: What does this skill change?
faq.answer: It directs the agent to perform available authorized work instead of sending users instructions for steps the agent can complete.

faq.question: Does it provide browser or API access?
faq.answer: No. It relies on tools, sessions, and permissions already available to the agent.

faq.question: Can the agent enter my password or verification code?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires users to enter passwords, keys, tokens, and one-time codes themselves.

faq.question: When must the agent ask for confirmation?
faq.answer: It must ask before irreversible or public actions, payments, and messages on your behalf, and for decisions reserved for you.

faq.question: What happens when a service session is closed?
faq.answer: The agent asks you to sign in through its browser, then continues with authorized tasks.

faq.question: How should completion be reported?
faq.answer: The agent verifies actions at their source, then reports completed work and any remaining user action in two lines.
